```{r}
source("R/read_jjm_text.R")

date_stamp <- format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y")
paths <- model_paths(root = "..", model = "1.14")
h2_rep_path <- file.path("..", "jjm", "assessment", "results", "h2_1.14.rep")
dat <- read_jjm_sections(paths$input)
h1_ctl <- read_jjm_sections(paths$h1_ctl)
h2_ctl <- read_jjm_sections(paths$h2_ctl)
h1_data <- read_jjm(paths$h1_ctl)$dat
h1_bio <- summarise_biology(h1_ctl)
h2_bio <- summarise_biology(h2_ctl)
model_years <- seq(as.numeric(dat$years[[1]]), as.numeric(dat$years[[2]]))
```

# Intro

This working paper evaluates the biological inputs used in the joint jack
mackerel assessment data and control files for model `1.14`. The immediate
purpose is to provide a focused biological-data review for `JM_SCW_prep`, while
keeping the assessment inputs and configuration files traceable to the
neighboring `jjm` repository.

This contribution extends from the 2022 Jack Mackerel Benchmark Workshop
(SCW14) and its final report, which provide the previous benchmark basis for
the joint jack mackerel assessment [@sprfmo2022scw14; @sprfmo2022scw14report].

Model `1.14` is the SC13 model update described in `jjm/assessment/README.md`
as model `1.13` with updates to historical weight-at-age for the Far North
fleet. The SC13 final report and Jack Mackerel Technical Annex provide the
formal assessment context for this model series [@sprfmo2025sc13report;
@sprfmo2025annex11]. The same data file is used with both assessment
hypotheses: `h1_1.14` for the single-stock model and `h2_1.14` for the
two-stock model.

# Model data

The source files used by this report are listed in @tbl-source-files.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-source-files
#| tbl-cap: "Source files used by this biological-data working paper."
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    role = c("Common data file", "Single-stock control file", "Two-stock control file"),
    path = unlist(paths, use.names = FALSE)
  ),
  col.names = c("Role", "Path")
)
```

The common data file defines the temporal, age, fleet, composition, index, and
weight-at-age information used by the model. The control files define how those
data are mapped to stock hypotheses, including natural mortality, maturity,
growth, population weight-at-age, catchability, and selectivity assumptions.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-data
#| tbl-cap: "High-level contents of the model 1.14 data file."
knitr::kable(summarise_model_data(dat))
```

The biological review should distinguish between information contained directly
in `1.14.dat` and assumptions introduced through the `h1_1.14.ctl` and
`h2_1.14.ctl` control files. This distinction matters because some biological
quantities are common to both stock hypotheses, while others differ by stock
hypothesis. @tbl-model-data summarizes the principal dimensions and named data
components in the common model `1.14` data file.

# Analyses

The analyses below are placeholders for reproducible checks against the model
`1.14` files. They are intentionally organized around the three biological data
questions requested for this working paper.

## Natural mortality

Natural mortality is configured in the control files under `#N_Mort`. The
single-stock model uses one natural mortality value, while the two-stock model
may assign stock-specific values. These configured values are shown in
@tbl-natural-mortality.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-natural-mortality
#| tbl-cap: "Natural mortality values configured for the model 1.14 stock hypotheses."
biology <- rbind(
  summarise_biology(h1_ctl)[, c("model", "stock", "natural_mortality")],
  summarise_biology(h2_ctl)[, c("model", "stock", "natural_mortality")]
)
knitr::kable(biology)
```

Items to evaluate:

1. Whether the assumed values are consistent with the biological basis used in
   previous benchmark and annual assessment documents.
2. Whether stock-specific assumptions in `h2_1.14` are supported by distinct
   biological evidence.
3. How sensitive derived spawning biomass and reference points are to plausible
   alternatives.

## Maturity

Maturity-at-age is configured in the control files under `#Pmatatage`. The
review should check whether the schedule is common or stock-specific, whether
age-1 partial maturity remains defensible, and whether the schedule aligns with
the biological source material used by the assessment.

In the JJM, maturity enters spawning biomass through a maturity-weighted
population weight-at-age vector. For stock $s$, year $y$, and age $a$, spawning
biomass is computed as

$$
SSB_{s,y} =
\sum_a
N_{s,y,a}
S_{s,y,a}^{(m_{\mathrm{spawn}} - 1) / 12}
w^{\mathrm{pop}}_{s,a}
p^{\mathrm{mat}}_{s,a},
$$

where $N_{s,y,a}$ is numbers-at-age at the start of year, $S_{s,y,a} =
\exp(-Z_{s,y,a})$ is annual survival, $m_{\mathrm{spawn}}$ is the spawning
month from `#Pspwn` in the data file, $w^{\mathrm{pop}}_{s,a}$ is the
population weight-at-age from `#Pwtatage`, and $p^{\mathrm{mat}}_{s,a}$ is
maturity-at-age from `#Pmatatage`. For model `1.14`, `#Pspwn` is 10.5, so the
spawning calculation occurs after $(10.5 - 1) / 12 = 0.792$ of annual mortality
has occurred.

The weight-at-age used in this equation is the stock-specific population
weight-at-age in the control file. It is fixed through time within each stock.
The time-varying fishery and index weight-at-age arrays in `1.14.dat`
(`Fwtatage` and `Iwtatage`) are used for predicted catch and index biomass, not
for spawning biomass.

For the two-stock `h2_1.14` model, the corresponding unfished spawning biomass
per recruit, multiplied by 1000, is 1597.8 for Stock 1 and 1367.3 for Stock 2.
These values use the stock-specific natural mortality, maturity-at-age, and
population weight-at-age schedules in `h2_1.14.ctl`, with spawning at month
10.5 and the age-12 plus group.
The age-specific contribution to those two values is shown in
@fig-h2-sbpr-at-age.

```{r}
#| label: fig-h2-sbpr-at-age
#| fig-cap: "Age-specific spawning biomass per recruit for the two stocks in h2_1.14, multiplied by 1000."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
h2_sbpr_at_age <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(h2_bio)), function(i) {
  natural_mortality <- h2_bio$natural_mortality[[i]]
  annual_survival <- exp(-natural_mortality)
  numbers_at_age <- numeric(12)
  numbers_at_age[[1]] <- 1
  for (age in 2:12) {
    numbers_at_age[[age]] <- numbers_at_age[[age - 1]] * annual_survival
  }
  numbers_at_age[[12]] <- numbers_at_age[[12]] / (1 - annual_survival)

  data.frame(
    stock = h2_bio$stock[[i]],
    age = seq_along(numbers_at_age),
    spawning_biomass = 1000 *
      numbers_at_age *
      exp(-natural_mortality * ((as.numeric(dat$Pspwn) - 1) / 12)) *
      h2_bio$population_weight_at_age[[i]] *
      h2_bio$maturity_at_age[[i]]
  )
}))

ggplot2::ggplot(
  h2_sbpr_at_age,
  ggplot2::aes(x = age, y = spawning_biomass, fill = stock)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7,
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 12, by = 1)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "age", y = "spawning biomass", fill = "Stock") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-maturity-preview
#| tbl-cap: "Maturity-at-age vectors read from the h2_1.14 control file."
make_vector_table <- function(x, value_name) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(x)), function(i) {
    values <- x[[value_name]][[i]]
    data.frame(
      model = x$model[[i]],
      stock = x$stock[[i]],
      age = seq_along(values),
      value = values
    )
  }))
}

mat_tbl <- make_vector_table(h2_bio, "maturity_at_age")
knitr::kable(mat_tbl)
```

The maturity-at-age schedules used in the spawning biomass calculation are
listed by stock for the two-stock model in @tbl-maturity-preview. The
single-stock model uses the same maturity schedule as Stock 1 in `h2_1.14`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ssb-weight-at-age
#| tbl-cap: "Population weight-at-age used with maturity-at-age in the h2_1.14 spawning biomass equation."
ssb_wt_tbl <- make_vector_table(h2_bio, "population_weight_at_age")
names(ssb_wt_tbl)[names(ssb_wt_tbl) == "value"] <- "population_weight_at_age"
knitr::kable(ssb_wt_tbl)
```

The population weight-at-age vectors paired with maturity in the spawning
biomass equation are shown for the two-stock model in @tbl-ssb-weight-at-age.
Again, the single-stock model uses the same vector as Stock 1 in `h2_1.14`.

## Weight-at-age

Weight-at-age is the central biological data issue for this working paper
because model `1.14` is specifically identified as updating historical
weight-at-age for the Far North fleet. The model includes population
weight-at-age in the control files and fishery or survey weight-at-age schedules
in the data file. The fixed population weight-at-age vectors used for spawning
biomass are repeated for `h2_1.14` in @tbl-pop-weight-at-age to separate them
from time-varying fishery and index weights-at-age.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pop-weight-at-age
#| tbl-cap: "Population weight-at-age vectors read from the h2_1.14 control file."
waa_tbl <- make_vector_table(h2_bio, "population_weight_at_age")
knitr::kable(waa_tbl)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
h1_weight_sources <- c(
  paste0("Fishery: ", h1_data$fsh_names),
  paste0("Index: ", h1_data$ind_names)
)
h1_weight_array <- array(
  NA_real_,
  dim = c(length(h1_weight_sources), h1_data$nyrs, h1_data$nages),
  dimnames = list(h1_weight_sources, model_years, seq_len(h1_data$nages))
)
h1_weight_array[seq_along(h1_data$fsh_names), , ] <- h1_data$wt_fsh
h1_weight_array[length(h1_data$fsh_names) + seq_along(h1_data$ind_names), , ] <- h1_data$wt_ind

h1_heatmap_sources <- !grepl("CPUE|DEPM", h1_weight_sources)

h1_weight_cor_by_age <- lapply(seq_len(h1_data$nages), function(age_index) {
  stats::cor(t(h1_weight_array[h1_heatmap_sources, , age_index]), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
})

h1_weight_cor_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(h1_weight_cor_by_age), function(age_index) {
  pairwise_cor <- h1_weight_cor_by_age[[age_index]][upper.tri(h1_weight_cor_by_age[[age_index]])]
  data.frame(
    age = age_index,
    mean_correlation = mean(pairwise_cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_correlation = stats::median(pairwise_cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum_correlation = min(pairwise_cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum_correlation = max(pairwise_cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    negative_pairs = sum(pairwise_cor < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    pairs_ge_0.7 = sum(pairwise_cor >= 0.7, na.rm = TRUE),
    pairs = sum(!is.na(pairwise_cor))
  )
}))

h1_weight_cor_summary_print <- h1_weight_cor_summary
h1_weight_cor_summary_print[, c(
  "mean_correlation", "median_correlation", "minimum_correlation", "maximum_correlation"
)] <- round(h1_weight_cor_summary_print[, c(
  "mean_correlation", "median_correlation", "minimum_correlation", "maximum_correlation"
)], 2)

h1_weight_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(h1_data$nages), function(age_index) {
  age_weights <- h1_weight_array[h1_heatmap_sources, , age_index, drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(
    source = rep(dimnames(age_weights)[[1]], each = h1_data$nyrs),
    gear_type = rep(sub(":.*$", "", dimnames(age_weights)[[1]]), each = h1_data$nyrs),
    source_label = rep(gsub("^(Fishery|Index): ", "", dimnames(age_weights)[[1]]), each = h1_data$nyrs),
    year = rep(model_years, times = sum(h1_heatmap_sources)),
    age = age_index,
    weight_at_age = as.vector(t(age_weights[, , 1]))
  )
}))
h1_weight_long$normalized_weight_at_age <- ave(
  h1_weight_long$weight_at_age,
  h1_weight_long$age,
  FUN = function(x) x / mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
)
h1_weight_long$gear_type <- factor(h1_weight_long$gear_type, levels = c("Fishery", "Index"))
h1_weight_long$source_label <- factor(
  h1_weight_long$source_label,
  levels = unique(h1_weight_long$source_label)
)

h1_age3_cor <- h1_weight_cor_by_age[[3]]
h1_age3_cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(h1_age3_cor))
names(h1_age3_cor_long) <- c("source_x", "source_y", "correlation")
h1_age3_pairs <- as.data.frame(t(h1_weight_array[h1_heatmap_sources, , 3]))
names(h1_age3_pairs) <- gsub("^(Fishery|Index): ", "", names(h1_age3_pairs))

h1_age8_cor <- h1_weight_cor_by_age[[8]]
h1_age8_cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(h1_age8_cor))
names(h1_age8_cor_long) <- c("source_x", "source_y", "correlation")

h1_age8_pairs <- as.data.frame(t(h1_weight_array[h1_heatmap_sources, , 8]))
names(h1_age8_pairs) <- gsub("^(Fishery|Index): ", "", names(h1_age8_pairs))
```

For the single-stock model `h1_1.14`, correlations among fishery and
acoustic-survey weight-at-age sources are generally modest across ages
(@tbl-waa-correlation-summary), with the age pattern shown in
@fig-waa-correlation-by-age. CPUE indices and DEPM are excluded because the CPUE
weights-at-age duplicate their associated fishery series and DEPM is omitted
here to simplify the source comparison.
The annual distributions of weight-at-age from this same reduced source set are
shown for ages 1-9 in @fig-waa-violin-by-age; the plotted points mark the
overall mean normalized weight-at-age for each source and age.
For age 3, the median cross-source correlation is
`r round(h1_weight_cor_summary$median_correlation[h1_weight_cor_summary$age == 3], 2)`,
with `r h1_weight_cor_summary$negative_pairs[h1_weight_cor_summary$age == 3]`
negative source pairs out of
`r h1_weight_cor_summary$pairs[h1_weight_cor_summary$age == 3]` total pairs.
The age-3 heatmap in @fig-age3-waa-correlation shows that several high
correlations are expected because some data sources share related biological
sampling and imputation histories. For age 3, `FarNorth` remains strongly
correlated with `Peru_Acoustic`. The same age-3 source subset is shown as a
pairs plot in @fig-age3-waa-pairs, with pairwise correlations in the upper
triangle and smoothed scatterplots in the lower triangle.
Age 8 has the highest mean pairwise correlation among the age-specific
weight-at-age series in @tbl-waa-correlation-summary; the corresponding
correlation heatmap for the same reduced source set is shown in
@fig-age8-waa-correlation. The same age-8 source subset is also shown as a
pairs plot in @fig-age8-waa-pairs, which makes the linearity and outlying years
behind the pairwise correlations easier to inspect.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-waa-correlation-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Pairwise correlations among h1_1.14 fishery and acoustic-survey weight-at-age time series, summarized by age. CPUE indices and DEPM are excluded."
gt::gt(h1_weight_cor_summary_print)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-waa-correlation-by-age

  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "age", y = "summary correlation") +
```

```{r}
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-age3-waa-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Pairs plot for h1_1.14 age-3 weight-at-age time series from the reduced fishery and acoustic-survey source set. Upper panels show pairwise correlations; lower panels show points and a smoother."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
panel_cor <- function(x, y, digits = 2, prefix = "r = ", cex.cor = 1.2, ...) {
  usr <- graphics::par("usr")
  on.exit(graphics::par(usr))
  graphics::par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  r <- stats::cor(x, y, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  label <- paste0(prefix, formatC(r, digits = digits, format = "f"))
  graphics::text(0.5, 0.5, label, cex = cex.cor)
}

panel_smooth <- function(x, y, ...) {
  graphics::points(
    x,
    y,
    pch = 16,
    cex = 0.45,
    col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#2f5d8c", alpha.f = 0.55)
  )
  smooth <- stats::lowess(x, y)
  graphics::lines(smooth, col = "#b64a3b", lwd = 1.5)
}

graphics::pairs(
  h1_age3_pairs,
  upper.panel = panel_cor,
  lower.panel = panel_smooth,
  diag.panel = NULL,
  gap = 0.35
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-age8-waa-correlation
#| fig-cap: "Pairwise correlations among h1_1.14 age-8 weight-at-age time series from fishery and acoustic-survey sources. CPUE indices and DEPM are excluded."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggplot2::ggplot(
  h1_age8_cor_long,
  ggplot2::aes(x = source_x, y = source_y, fill = correlation)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +

    low = "#3b6fb6",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#b64a3b",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1),
    name = "r"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_equal() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
```
```{r}
  )
```

Items to evaluate:

1. Which `1.14.dat` sections contain Far North fishery and associated index
   weight-at-age schedules.
2. How the historical Far North updates differ from model `1.13`.
3. Whether population, fishery, and survey weight-at-age schedules are
   internally consistent.
4. Whether the updated historical weights change the biological interpretation
   of catch biomass, spawning biomass, or stock-specific productivity.

# Results and discussion

This section should synthesize the biological checks rather than repeat the full
assessment model description. The expected output is a concise judgement on
whether the biological inputs in model `1.14` are internally consistent,
adequately documented, and suitable as the basis for the `JM_SCW_prep` working
paper package.

The age-structured contribution to estimated spawning biomass from the fitted
`h2_1.14` model is shown in @fig-h2-ssb-age-timeseries. Age groups 7 and older
are pooled to keep the time series interpretable while retaining the dominant
older-age contribution. Stock 1 has a broader distribution across ages, with
substantial contributions from ages 2-5 and a smaller relative contribution from
the pooled older ages in recent years. Stock 2 is shifted older because age-1
fish are immature and age-2 maturity is partial; its spawning biomass is
therefore concentrated more strongly in ages 3-6 and the 7+ group, with the 7+
group contributing a larger share than in Stock 1.

The same fitted spawning biomass time series is shown by stock in
@fig-h2-ssb-stock-scale. The purpose of this second figure is to show the
relative scale of spawning biomass between the two stocks.

```{r}
#| label: fig-h2-ssb-age-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "Age-structured contribution to estimated spawning biomass from the fitted h2_1.14 model. Ages 7 and older are pooled."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
h2_ssb_contribution <- read_h2_spawning_contribution(
  rep_path = h2_rep_path,
  h2_bio = h2_bio,
  years = model_years,
  spawn_month = as.numeric(dat$Pspwn)
)

h2_ssb_contribution$age_group <- ifelse(
  h2_ssb_contribution$age >= 7,
  "7+",
  as.character(h2_ssb_contribution$age)
)
h2_ssb_contribution$age_group <- factor(
  h2_ssb_contribution$age_group,
  levels = c(as.character(1:6), "7+")
)

h2_ssb_age_plot <- aggregate(
  spawning_biomass ~ stock + year + age_group,
  data = h2_ssb_contribution,
  FUN = sum
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  h2_ssb_age_plot,
  ggplot2::aes(x = year, y = spawning_biomass, fill = age_group)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ stock, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(model_years), max(model_years), by = 5)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "year", y = "spawning biomass contribution", fill = "Age") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-h2-ssb-stock-scale
#| fig-cap: "Stacked spawning biomass by stock from the fitted h2_1.14 model. This figure is intended to show the relative scale between stocks."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
h2_ssb_stock_plot <- aggregate(
  spawning_biomass ~ stock + year,
  data = h2_ssb_contribution,
  FUN = sum
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  h2_ssb_stock_plot,
  ggplot2::aes(x = year, y = spawning_biomass, fill = stock)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_area(alpha = 0.9, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(model_years), max(model_years), by = 5)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "year", y = "spawning biomass", fill = "Stock") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

Initial points to carry forward:

1. The authoritative files remain in `jjm/assessment`; this repository reads
   them directly for reproducibility.
2. The single-stock and two-stock hypotheses share the same common data file but
   differ in biological and stock-structure assumptions through their control
   files.
3. The Far North historical weight-at-age update should be evaluated explicitly
   against model `1.13`, because that is the defining change from `1.13` to
   `1.14`.
